quests.question: They spend every Saturday morning playing ___ tennis at the park.
quests.sentence: They spend every Saturday morning playing ___ tennis at the park.
quests.hint: This is a sport name, which usually stands alone.
quests.explanation: 'Tennis' is a sport name, and sport names take no article when talking about playing them in general.

quests.question: A courier dropped off a small parcel this morning. ___ parcel was addressed to my roommate, not me.
quests.sentence: A courier dropped off a small parcel this morning. ___ parcel was addressed to my roommate, not me.
quests.hint: This refers back to the exact parcel just mentioned.
quests.explanation: 'The parcel' refers back to the one already introduced in the first sentence, so it takes 'the'.

quests.question: She's pursuing ___ union role within the company to advocate for workers' rights.
quests.sentence: She's pursuing ___ union role within the company to advocate for workers' rights.
quests.hint: This word starts with the same tricky glide sound as 'uniform'.
quests.explanation: 'Union' begins with a 'y' glide consonant sound, even though it's spelled with the vowel letter 'u', so it takes 'a'.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound

quests.question: He's been away at ___ college since September, studying marketing.
quests.sentence: He's been away at ___ college since September, studying marketing.
quests.hint: This describes his situation as a student, not a specific building.
quests.explanation: 'At college' is a fixed institutional expression meaning being a student, so it takes no article.

quests.question: This is without question ___ hardest exam I've taken all semester.
quests.sentence: This is without question ___ hardest exam I've taken all semester.
quests.hint: This adjective compares the exam against every other one you've taken.
quests.explanation: 'Hardest' is a superlative comparing this exam to every other one this semester, so it takes 'the'.

quests.question: Could you hand me ___ glass from the top shelf?
quests.sentence: Could you hand me ___ glass from the top shelf?
quests.hint: This is one countable drinking vessel, not the material.
quests.explanation: Here 'glass' means a drinking vessel, a countable object, so it takes 'a' — a different meaning from the uncountable material sense.
quests.grammarRule: Countable meaning of a normally uncountable noun

quests.question: The museum recently acquired ___ extremely rare, centuries-old manuscript from a private collector.
quests.sentence: The museum recently acquired ___ extremely rare, centuries-old manuscript from a private collector.
quests.hint: Focus only on the word right after the gap, even with a long chain of description following.
quests.explanation: 'Extremely' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an', regardless of how many more words describe the manuscript afterward.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a vowel sound

quests.question: We'll confirm the details by ___ email later today.
quests.sentence: We'll confirm the details by ___ email later today.
quests.hint: This describes a method of communication, similar to 'by phone' or 'by mail'.
quests.explanation: 'By email' is a fixed expression describing a method of communication and takes no article.

quests.question: ___ good password should never be reused across different websites.
quests.sentence: ___ good password should never be reused across different websites.
quests.hint: This describes passwords as a category, not one specific one.
quests.explanation: 'A good password' here represents passwords in general, a generic statement about what any good password should be like.

quests.question: We finally boarded our flight, and ___ flight attendants welcomed us warmly as we found our seats.
quests.sentence: We finally boarded our flight, and ___ flight attendants welcomed us warmly as we found our seats.
quests.hint: Once boarding a flight is mentioned, this role is automatically understood.
quests.explanation: 'The flight attendants' is inferred from the situation of boarding a flight, the same bridging reasoning used in earlier levels.
quests.grammarRule: Bridging inference from an established scenario

quests.question: The bakery just opened its ___ second location downtown.
quests.sentence: The bakery just opened its ___ second location downtown.
quests.hint: Is this identifying a position in a known sequence, or simply counting a new addition?
quests.explanation: This 'second' just counts a new addition rather than identifying a position in an existing, known sequence, so it takes 'a'.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound

quests.question: He ordered ___ same drink he always gets, without even looking at the menu.
quests.sentence: He ordered ___ same drink he always gets, without even looking at the menu.
quests.hint: This special word always pairs with one particular article.
quests.explanation: 'The same' is a fixed expression that always takes 'the', regardless of what noun follows it.

quests.question: It takes ___ courage to admit when you're wrong.
quests.sentence: It takes ___ courage to admit when you're wrong.
quests.hint: This is a quality in general, not one specific instance of it.
quests.explanation: 'Courage' here is an uncountable, abstract concept discussed in general, so it takes no article.

quests.question: I really respected ___ courage she showed during the interview.
quests.sentence: I really respected ___ courage she showed during the interview.
quests.hint: This isn't courage in general — it's the specific courage from one particular moment.
quests.explanation: Even though 'courage' is usually article-free, once it refers to one specific, identified instance, it takes 'the', the same pattern seen with 'advice' and 'wisdom'.

quests.question: It would be ___ honor to work alongside someone so experienced.
quests.sentence: It would be ___ honor to work alongside someone so experienced.
quests.hint: The 'h' at the start of this word is silent.
quests.explanation: 'Honor' has a silent 'h', so it's pronounced starting with a vowel sound and takes 'an'.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a vowel sound

quests.question: One of ___ classrooms on this floor doesn't have working air conditioning.
quests.sentence: One of ___ classrooms on this floor doesn't have working air conditioning.
quests.hint: This fixed pattern always pairs with the same article before the plural noun.
quests.explanation: 'One of the classrooms' is a fixed pattern that always uses 'the' before the plural noun, selecting one member from an already-defined group.
quests.grammarRule: Fixed pattern: one of the [plural noun]

quests.question: Only ___ single employee showed up early for the meeting.
quests.sentence: Only ___ single employee showed up early for the meeting.
quests.hint: This introduces one new, unidentified person, not a member of a defined group.
quests.explanation: This simply introduces one unidentified employee, so it takes 'a' — 'single' begins with a consonant sound.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound

quests.question: We tested four different designs. Three failed, and ___ last one finally worked.
quests.sentence: We tested four different designs. Three failed, and ___ last one finally worked.
quests.hint: Once three have been accounted for, the final one becomes identifiable.
quests.explanation: 'The last one' refers to the remaining, now-identifiable member of the group of four already mentioned, so it takes 'the'.
quests.grammarRule: Definite by elimination from a known set

quests.question: They rented ___ outdoor basketball court for the tournament.
quests.sentence: They rented ___ outdoor basketball court for the tournament.
quests.hint: This is a new, unspecified sports facility, and the word right after the gap starts with a vowel sound.
quests.explanation: 'Outdoor' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'. This is also a new, unidentified court being introduced here.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a vowel sound

quests.question: ___ octopus is remarkably intelligent for an invertebrate.
quests.sentence: ___ octopus is remarkably intelligent for an invertebrate.
quests.hint: This describes the whole species in a formal, general way.
quests.explanation: A singular noun with 'the' can represent an entire species in a formal general statement, the same generic pattern used with 'the dolphin' and 'the elephant'.

quests.question: Usually the traffic isn't bad, but today specifically, ___ traffic on the highway was unbearable.
quests.sentence: Usually the traffic isn't bad, but today specifically, ___ traffic on the highway was unbearable.
quests.hint: The word 'specifically' signals a shift from the general idea mentioned first.
quests.explanation: 'Today specifically' signals a shift from a general statement to one specific, identified instance, so it takes 'the'.

quests.question: We rarely eat ___ lunch together during the week because of our schedules.
quests.sentence: We rarely eat ___ lunch together during the week because of our schedules.
quests.hint: This is a meal name, which usually stands alone.
quests.explanation: 'Lunch' is a meal name and takes no article in everyday statements like this one.

quests.question: She recently earned ___ PhD in molecular biology.
quests.sentence: She recently earned ___ PhD in molecular biology.
quests.hint: Say the name of the first letter out loud, not the letter itself.
quests.explanation: 'PhD' is pronounced letter by letter, and 'P' is said as 'pee', which starts with a consonant sound, so it takes 'a'.
quests.grammarRule: Article choice with acronyms by pronunciation

quests.question: He's looking for ___ apartment that allows pets.
quests.sentence: He's looking for ___ apartment that allows pets.
quests.hint: This describes a general type of apartment, not one specific one he has in mind.
quests.explanation: 'An apartment that allows pets' describes a general type he's searching for, not one particular apartment already identified, so it takes 'an' — 'apartment' begins with a vowel sound.

quests.question: Critics agree that this is ___ most ambitious project the studio has ever attempted.
quests.sentence: Critics agree that this is ___ most ambitious project the studio has ever attempted.
quests.hint: This ranks the project above every other one the studio has made.
quests.explanation: 'Most ambitious' is a superlative phrase, so it takes 'the', regardless of the clause that follows it.

quests.question: Her father spent several years in ___ prison during his youth, and it changed his outlook on life.
quests.sentence: Her father spent several years in ___ prison during his youth, and it changed his outlook on life.
quests.hint: This describes his situation as an inmate, not a specific building.
quests.explanation: 'In prison' describes the institutional situation of being incarcerated, so it takes no article.

quests.question: The city built a new library two years ago. Attendance at ___ library has grown steadily ever since.
quests.sentence: The city built a new library two years ago. Attendance at ___ library has grown steadily ever since.
quests.hint: This refers back to the exact library already mentioned, even after some time has passed.
quests.explanation: 'The library' still refers back to the one introduced in the first sentence, even though some time has passed within the story — anaphoric reference doesn't expire.

quests.question: This isn't ___ good time to talk — can I call you back later?
quests.sentence: This isn't ___ good time to talk — can I call you back later?
quests.hint: This means one specific occasion or moment, not time in the abstract.
quests.explanation: When 'time' means a specific occasion, it becomes countable, so it takes 'a' — 'good' begins with a consonant sound.
quests.grammarRule: Countable meaning of a normally uncountable noun

quests.question: After the long trial finally ended, ___ jury took less than an hour to reach a verdict.
quests.sentence: After the long trial finally ended, ___ jury took less than an hour to reach a verdict.
quests.hint: Once a trial is mentioned, this group is automatically understood.
quests.explanation: 'The jury' is inferred from the situation of a trial, the same bridging reasoning used throughout the curriculum.
quests.grammarRule: Bridging inference from an established scenario

quests.question: ___ successful entrepreneur must be willing to take calculated risks.
quests.sentence: ___ successful entrepreneur must be willing to take calculated risks.
quests.hint: This describes entrepreneurs as a category, not one particular person.
quests.explanation: 'A successful entrepreneur' here represents entrepreneurs in general, a generic statement about what it takes to succeed in that category.
